agree.reason: The safety program and the 20-to-12-hour training rewrite would make a skeptical HR manager take her seriously, but the letter leaves out her strongest evidence on regulated recordkeeping, so the 'teacher who doesn't know a plant' doubt only partly goes away.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported claim about cutting training time in half, but 'roughly 1,000 students' is an estimate the brief doesn't state, and saying the newly trained teachers' labs have 'the same safety record' stretches the facts a little.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out a student total, but it never states that 20 to 12 hours is a 40% cut, never adds up the roughly a dozen teachers she has trained, and gives the AP numbers without a relative gain or any link to the job.

right_comparison.reason: Before-and-after figures appear for the training hours and the AP pass rate, but the letter never compares her with the real alternative, a candidate who has GMP experience, and never ties that comparison to the audited record-keeping she already does.

qualification.reason: The GMP course has a checkable completion date of May 2, but the letter never mentions the June 14 earliest start, which the reader needs, and says nothing about what happens if the course or the LMS learning falls short.

objections.reason: It names the GMP records gap but answers it only with a course, and leaves out the signed training records and two clean state audits, which answer the objection directly.

fit.reason: It is a properly addressed one-page cover letter at a suitable length, with only the clumsy 'I can also show results' paragraph out of place.
